Composite: Alamy/Getty images/The Guardian Glastonbury festival Sam Fender, Harry Styles and Billie Eilish to be youngest Glastonbury headliners of 21st century
 Cher will take the legends slot at next year’s festival, which will also see debuts from Kraftwerk and Angine de Poitrine
 Read the lineup so far in full below
 Laura Snapes Wed 18 Nov 2026 03.00 EST Last modified on Wed 18 Nov 2026 03.46 EST Share Prefer the Guardian on Google After fervent speculation about its headliners, the first batch of 2027 Glastonbury performers has been announced, and with it the youngest cohort of headliners this century.
 This year’s edition brings two debut turns atop the Pyramid stage: North Shields singer-songwriter Sam Fender on Friday, and former boyband star turned global supernova Harry Styles on Saturday.
 Closing Sunday night is a relative Glastonbury veteran despite her young age: US pop star Billie Eilish headlines for a second time, after becoming the festival’s youngest solo headliner in 2022 and making her festival debut on the Other stage in 2019.
 By next June, Fender and Styles will both be 33 years old, and Eilish 25.
 Fender previously had to pull out of playing the festival in 2019 and was due to play the cancelled 2020 edition; he performed second to Eilish on the Pyramid stage in 2022. It is Styles’ first time at the festival as a performer; the press materials note that he enjoyed the event as a punter in 2025.
 In a true coup for the festival, Cher will make an unexpected appearance in this year’s Sunday afternoon legends slot, despite not having toured since 2020 and claiming to have released her final album in 2024.
 View image in fullscreen In a coup for the festival, Cher will make an unexpected appearance in this year’s Sunday afternoon legends slot. Photograph: Andreas Rentz/Getty Images Next year’s festival is the first since 2025: Glastonbury took one of its semi-regular fallow years in 2026 to allow Worthy farm to recover. “We are so happy to be coming back after our fallow year and, as we head into winter after that peaceful period, we wanted to give you an early musical taster of what’s to come at Glastonbury 2027 with this spread of incredible artists,” festival organiser Emily Eavis said in a statement.
 “We are beyond excited about how it’s all shaping up. We will bring you even more names in the new year and can’t wait to see you down here on Worthy farm in June for some much-needed good times.”
 Kraftwerk will also play for the first time when they headline the West Holts stage.
 Hot off the back of a flush of Grammy nominations, Québécois microtonal rock duo Angine de Poitrine will make their Glastonbury debut, as will the similarly garlanded Womack Sisters. Slovakian pop star Adéla, Manchester DJ Josh Baker, London soul singer Sienna Spiro and US artist Sombr also play for the first time.
 From burning bogs to boutique bonanzas: how did Britain become a nation of festival obsessives? Read more London trio the xx are set to return around the release of their as-yet unannounced fourth album. Lily Allen, Little Simz, Chase and Status, Massive Attack, Ezra Collective and FKA twigs are also among the big returning names.
 Pop fans will be sated by appearances from Blood Orange, Christine and the Queens – who broke the UK as a result of his galvanising 2016 set, the morning after the Brexit vote – Chvrches, Ellie Goulding, Flo, Kacey Musgraves, Keo, Leon Bridges, Lianne La Havas, Lola Young, Nao, Robyn, Skye Newman, Teddy Swims, Texas, Thee Sacred Souls, Thundercat and Underscores.
 View image in fullscreen Khn of Québécois duo Angine de Poitrine Photograph: José Sena Goulão/EPA While Glastonbury rarely tends to the heavy end of rock, guitar fans may flock to sets from Crowded House, Dinosaur Jr, Florence Road, Getdown Services, Jamie T, Kingfishr, King Gizzard and the Lizard Wizard, Primal Scream, Saint Etienne, the War on Drugs, Westside Cowboy and Wunderhorse.
 Glastonbury’s typically globe-trotting bill brings in J-pop band Atarashii Gakko!, South African stars Ecca Vandal and Moonchild Sanelly, New Zealand reggae act Fat Freddy’s Drop and Tuareg rock band Tinariwen.

 So far, the festival’s rap credentials come from De La Soul, Mike D, the Streets and Young Fathers, while in dance, the Avalanches, Basement Jaxx, Bonobo, Confidence Man, Hot Chip – practically the Glastonbury house band – Nia Archives, Sammy Virji and Underworld will be upping revellers’ step counts.
 The 2027 edition of the festival will mark the first time that ticket prices have broken the £400 mark, clocking in at £408 (including a £5 booking fee), up from £378.50 in 2025.
 View image in fullscreen Young Fathers performing in 2018. Photograph: Burak Çıngı/Redferns Tickets went on sale on 4 October and sold out in minutes. Emily Eavis previously clarified that contrary to rumours, Madonna would not be headlining off the back of her acclaimed Confessions II album.
 Festival founder Michael Eavis stepped back from the day-to-day running of the festival several years ago, and recently celebrated his 91st birthday.
 Next year’s Glastonbury will be hoping to avoid the controversy of 2025’s edition, when police investigated punk duo Bob Vylan after they chanted “death, death to the IDF” – the Israel Defense Forces – on the West Holts stage. The investigation was dropped in December.
